title: The Digital Hive and the End of a Common World
gist: Roughly 40 percent of US adults rely on Facebook or YouTube for news, where engagement-optimized short clips and influencer commentary replace accountable journalism. The author argues this 'digital hive', combined with collapsing media trust (28 percent per Gallup) and the loss of local newspapers, rewards divisive rhetoric and erodes a shared factual baseline.

insights.claim: Media trust did not vanish but realigned when the network news oligopoly fragmented: audiences of Newsmax, Breitbart, and One America News Network trust those outlets while distrusting the New York Times and CNN.

insights.so_what: Erosion of shared facts raises the risk of policy unpredictability and social instability that markets must price.
